literal: Having already attained the utmost rank of chief minister, with domains surpassing Qi and Lu, could indulgence in nurturing him still be excessive?
idiomatic: Once he stood at the summit of power, with domains exceeding those of Qi and Lu, how could further indulgence still be called going too far?

literal: But his heart was like fierce fire; mountains and forests could not supply its violence;
idiomatic: Yet his heart blazed like wildfire, and no mountain forest could satisfy its fury;

literal: his intent was like a leaking cup; rivers and streams could not fill its overflow.
idiomatic: his ambition was like a cup that never holds still—no river could slake its excess.

literal: When arms and armor had grown somewhat quiet and the regions gradually at peace, he did not extend heaven's achievement but kept it for himself alone; in granting and taking he followed his whim, in praise and blame he acted at will—the traces of one without a lord grew daily more evident.
idiomatic: When war subsided and the realm grew calm again, he claimed heaven's merit as his own; rewards and punishments obeyed his whim, and his lordless conduct grew plainer by the day.

literal: To count his crimes by plucking hairs would scarcely suffice;
idiomatic: To number his crimes hair by hair would still fall short;

literal: to record his guilt by cutting bamboo could never exhaust it.
idiomatic: and to inscribe his guilt on bamboo slips could never exhaust the list.

literal: Again he borrowed the name of court orthodoxy while secretly plotting rebellion, casting sidelong glances at the imperial residence and coveting the sacred succession.
idiomatic: Again he cloaked himself in loyalty to the court while plotting treason in secret, eyeing the imperial palace and coveting the throne.

literal: He harbored a heart to tear the crown and destroy the regalia, and meant to uproot the tree and block the source.
idiomatic: He harbored the will to tear down the crown and regalia and to uproot the dynasty at its source.

literal: Heaven had already grown weary of disorder, and men too repented the calamity; ministers who shared his evil secretly came to report.
idiomatic: Heaven had grown weary of chaos and men repented the disaster; accomplices came forward in secret to denounce him.

literal: A general who rebels must be executed; his guilt admits no pardon.
idiomatic: A rebel commander must die; his crimes allow no mercy.

literal: Moreover Yuan Tianmu was a junior branch of the imperial clan, of slight repute by name; meeting with the moment's chance, he took part in the righteous rising.
idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu too belonged to a junior line of the house, a man of little standing who had joined the loyal rising when fortune offered the chance.

literal: He could not exhaust his loyalty to serve the state and kin, but again abandoned the root to chase the branch, turned his back on allies to join the alien side, became their strategist, and completed their wicked design.
idiomatic: He failed to give his full loyalty to throne and clan, turned from the root to chase the branch, betrayed his allies for the enemy, became their strategist, and helped fulfill their treacherous design.

literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be forgiven!
idiomatic: If this could be tolerated, what crime could not?

literal: Both were executed for their crimes and brought ruin on themselves.
idiomatic: Both were put to death for their crimes and brought calamity on themselves.

literal: The chief villain having been removed, men and spirits rejoiced in peace; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: With the chief villain gone, men and spirits rejoiced; a general amnesty was proclaimed for all under heaven.

literal: Guard-General of Martial Readiness Xi Yi and former Inspector of Former Yan Province Cui Yuan were dispatched to lead troops and garrison North Zhong.
idiomatic: Xi Yi, guard-general of martial readiness, and Cui Yuan, former inspector of Former Yan province, were sent with troops to garrison North Zhong.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: That night, Vice Director Erzhu Shilong, Rong's wife the Princess of Xiang Commandery, and others led Rong's troops to burn the Xiyang Gate, went out, and encamped at Heyin.
idiomatic: That night Vice Director Erzhu Shilong, Rong's wife the Princess of Xiang Commandery, and others led Rong's retainers to burn the Xiyang Gate, left the city, and encamped at Heyin.

literal: On jihai day they attacked Hey Bridge, captured Yi and the others on the road and killed them, held North Zhong city, and pressed south on the capital.
idiomatic: On jihai they attacked Hey Bridge, seized Yi and his party on the march and killed them, occupied North Zhong, and pressed the capital from the south.

literal: An edict made Erzhu Tianguang, general of agile cavalry, inspector of Yong Province, and Duke of Guangzong with an open state, director of the Masters of Writing with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies; and Yang Jin, director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the State of the Grandee, bearer of the staff of office, commissioner with full powers, commander of the nine provinces Bing, Xi, Yan, Heng, Yun, Shuo, Xian, Fen, and Yu, general of agile cavalry, inspector of Bing Province, and concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, northern-route grand mobile office, to manage Bing and Xi.
idiomatic: An edict appointed Erzhu Tianguang, general of agile cavalry, inspector of Yong province, and duke of Guangzong with an open state, as director of the Masters of Writing with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies; and Yang Jin, director of the Masters of Writing and state grandee, bearer of the staff of office, as commissioner with full powers over Bing, Xi, Yan, Heng, Yun, Shuo, Xian, Fen, and Yu, general of agile cavalry, inspector of Bing province, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and northern-route grand mobile office, to manage Bing and Xi.

literal: On gengzi day an edict ordered all men of the old Xianbei registration to come to Hualin Park; the emperor would personally review and assign them.
idiomatic: On gengzi an edict summoned all men of the old Xianbei registration to Hualin Park for the emperor's personal review.

literal: General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Gao Qianyong was made director of the Masters of Writing and grand envoy of Hebei, to gather fierce warriors.
idiomatic: Gao Qianyong, general who pacifies the army and grand master of splendid happiness, was made director of the Masters of Writing and grand envoy of Hebei to gather fierce warriors.

literal: Tenth month of winter, new moon on guimao day: General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Yuan Baoju was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang; Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and Duke of Ruyang with an open state Yuan Xiu as Prince of Pingyang; Regular Attendant and General of the Dragon Cavalry Yuan Dan, Baron of Xinyang with an open state, as Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the guimao new moon, Yuan Baoju, general who pacifies the south and grand master of splendid happiness, was enfeoffed as prince of Nanyang; Yuan Xiu, grand director of the imperial clan and duke of Ruyang with an open state, as prince of Pingyang; and Yuan Dan, regular attendant and general of the dragon cavalry, baron of Xinyang with an open state, as prince of Changle.

literal: Again restored Regular Attendant and Duke of Langye with an open state.
idiomatic: Regular Attendant and Duke of Langye with an open state were also restored.

literal: Li Shuren's office and rank, [12] and he remained commissioner with full powers and grand commander to attack Shilong.
idiomatic: Li Shuren's office and rank [12] were restored, and he remained commissioner with full powers and grand commander to attack Shilong.

literal: Prince of Wei Commandery Chen was transferred to Prince of Zhao Commandery; Chen's nephew, Prince of Zhao Commandery Zhi, was changed to Prince of Pingchang.
idiomatic: Prince of Wei Commandery Chen was re-enfeoffed as prince of Zhao Commandery; his nephew Zhi, prince of Zhao Commandery, was made prince of Pingchang instead.

literal: Bearer of ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies Li Qian died.
idiomatic: Li Qian, bearer of ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, died.

literal: On dingwei day recruitment placards for attacking Hey Bridge were issued; rewards in silk and appointment to office varied by rank.
idiomatic: On dingwei recruitment placards for the assault on Hey Bridge were posted, with graded rewards in silk and offices.

literal: On wushen day a prince was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed, and civil and military officials of the hundred offices all received two grades of promotion.
idiomatic: On wushen a prince was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed and every civil and military official received two grades of promotion.

literal: Pacification-General of the South and Director of the Masters of Writing Wei Langen was made concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing and Hebei mobile office; Ding, Xiang, and Yin provinces were placed under Langen's command.
idiomatic: Wei Langen, pacification-general of the south and director of the Masters of Writing, was made concurrent left vice director and Hebei mobile office commander; Ding, Xiang, and Yin provinces were placed under his command.

literal: On yimao day Regular Attendant and Acting Pacification-General of the West and Commander Li Miao burned Hey Bridge with fire-ships; Erzhu Shilong withdrew.
idiomatic: On yimao Li Miao, regular attendant, acting pacification-general of the west, and commander, burned Hey Bridge with fire-ships and Erzhu Shilong retreated.

literal: On bingchen day an edict ordered Grand Commander and Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Office Yuan Zigong to lead ten thousand foot and horse out by the western route; Mobile Office Yang Yu to lead Commander Li Kanxi and others' levies of eight thousand brave men by the eastern route, to defend and attack them.
idiomatic: On bingchen an edict ordered Yuan Zigong, grand commander, concurrent vice director, and mobile office commander, to lead ten thousand foot and horse by the western route; Yang Yu of the mobile office to lead Li Kanxi and other commanders' levies of eight thousand brave men by the eastern route, to defend and attack them.

literal: Zigong still garrisoned Dangu of Mount Taihang.
idiomatic: Zigong continued to garrison Dangu on Mount Taihang.

literal: Shilong reached Jian Province; Inspector Lu Xizhi held out in defense; the city fell and all were slaughtered, only Xizhi being spared.
idiomatic: Shilong reached Jian province; Inspector Lu Xizhi defended the city; when it fell the population was slaughtered, Xizhi alone being spared.

literal: General of the Center Army and former Inspector of East Jing Province Yuan Xiangong was made commissioner with full powers, commander of the three provinces Jin, Jian, and South Fen, Pacification-General of the West, inspector of Jin Province, and concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing, western-campaign-route grand mobile office, [13] commanding the supervisors Xue Shanle, Xue Xiuyi, Pei Yuanjun, Xue Chongli, Xue Xizu, and others.
idiomatic: Yuan Xiangong, general of the center army and former inspector of East Jing province, was made commissioner with full powers over Jin, Jian, and South Fen, pacification-general of the west, inspector of Jin province, concurrent left vice director, and western-campaign-route grand mobile office, [13] with command over Xue Shanle, Xue Xiuyi, Pei Yuanjun, Xue Chongli, Xue Xizu, and the other supervisors.

literal: On dingmao day an edict stated that because Shilong had rebelled in the north and Heyin was held firm in defense, all commanders, generals, civil and military officials in the city should receive two grades of promotion, and soldiers three years' exemption from corvée.
idiomatic: On dingmao an edict declared that because Shilong had rebelled in the north while Heyin held firm, every commander, general, and civil or military official in the city should receive two grades of promotion and soldiers three years' exemption from corvée.

literal: On renshen day Erzhu Shilong halted at Gaodu of Jianxing; Erzhu Zhao came from Jinyang to join him; together they made Taiyuan Administrator and acting Inspector of Bing Province Yuan Ye, Prince of Changguang, their leader, proclaimed a general amnesty in their territory, era name Jianming, and a universal promotion of four grades.
idiomatic: On renshen Erzhu Shilong halted at Gaodu in Jianxing; Erzhu Zhao came from Jinyang to join him; together they set Yuan Ye, prince of Changguang, who was Taiyuan administrator and acting inspector of Bing province, at their head, proclaimed a general amnesty in their territory, era name Jianming, and a universal promotion of four grades.

literal: Inspector of Xu Province Erzhu Zhongyuan rebelled and led his host toward the capital.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan, inspector of Xu province, rebelled and marched his army toward the capital.

literal: Eleventh month, new moon on guiyou day: an edict made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Guard-General Zheng Xianhu commissioner with full powers, grand general, and grand commander, to go with Commander Li Kanxi to Mobile Office Yang Yu to attack him.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the guiyou new moon, an edict made Zheng Xianhu, general of chariots and cavalry and left guard-general, commissioner with full powers, grand general, and grand commander, to go with Li Kanxi to Yang Yu's mobile office to attack him.

literal: On yihai day Bearer of the Staff of Office, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Western-Route Grand Mobile Office, and Duke of the State of the Grandee Changsun Zhi was made Duke of the Grandee; Director of the Masters of Writing, General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Office with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and Prince of Huaiyang Yu was made Duke of the State of the Grandee.
idiomatic: On yihai Changsun Zhi, bearer of the staff of office, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, western-route grand mobile office, and state grandee, was made grand duke; and Yu, prince of Huaiyang, director of the Masters of Writing, general of agile cavalry, and opener of the office with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, was made state grandee.

literal: On bingzi day Erzhu Tianguang, general of agile cavalry, bearer of ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, inspector of Yong Province, and Duke of Guangzong with an open state, opened an office and was advanced in rank to prince.
idiomatic: On bingzi Erzhu Tianguang, general of agile cavalry, bearer of ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, inspector of Yong province, and duke of Guangzong with an open state, opened an office and was advanced to prince.

literal: On dingchou day Erzhu Zhongyuan took West Yan Province and seized Inspector Wang Yan.
idiomatic: On dingchou Erzhu Zhongyuan took West Yan province and seized Wang Yan, inspector.

literal: On guiwei day Right Guard-General Heluo Sheng was made eastern-expedition commander.
idiomatic: On guiwei Heluo Sheng, right guard-general, was made eastern-expedition commander.

literal: On renchen day Left Guard-General and Grand Commander Zheng Xianhu was also made concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing and mobile office commander, to join Sheng in attacking Zhongyuan.
idiomatic: On renchen Zheng Xianhu, left guard-general and grand commander, was also made concurrent left vice director and mobile office commander to join Sheng in attacking Zhongyuan.

literal: On wuxu day an edict abolished Wei Langen's mobile office; Rear-General and Inspector of Ding Province Xue Tanshang was made commissioner with full powers and concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, northern-route mobile office, to levy troops as circumstances required.
idiomatic: On wuxu an edict abolished Wei Langen's mobile office; Xue Tanshang, rear-general and inspector of Ding province, was made commissioner with full powers, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and northern-route mobile office commander, to levy troops as needed.

literal: Acting Inspector of Yu Province Yuan Chongli killed the later acting provincial officer Yin Daohe and seized Yu Province on his own authority.
idiomatic: Yuan Chongli, acting inspector of Yu province, killed Yin Daohe, who had been acting in provincial affairs, and seized Yu province on his own authority.

literal: On gengzi day Heluo Sheng fought Zhongyuan east of Huatai, was defeated, and then fled to join him.
idiomatic: On gengzi Heluo Sheng fought Zhongyuan east of Huatai, was defeated, and then went over to his side.

literal: Twelfth month, new moon on renyin day: Erzhu Zhao raided Dangu; Supervisor Cui Bofeng died in battle; Supervisors Yang Wenyi and Shi Wulong surrendered to Zhao; Grand Commander Yuan Zigong fled in retreat.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the renyin new moon, Erzhu Zhao raided Dangu; Cui Bofeng, supervisor, was killed in battle; Yang Wenyi and Shi Wulong, supervisors, surrendered to Zhao; Yuan Zigong, grand commander, fled.

literal: On jiachen day Erzhu Zhao and Erzhu Dulü from Fuping Ford upstream led cavalry across the ford to strike the capital.
idiomatic: On jiachen Erzhu Zhao and Erzhu Dulü crossed from Fuping Ford upstream with cavalry to strike the capital.

literal: The affair arose in sudden haste; the palace guard could not hold.
idiomatic: Caught by sudden crisis, the palace guard could not hold.

literal: The emperor went out through the Cloud Dragon Gate.
idiomatic: The emperor fled out through the Cloud Dragon Gate.

literal: Zhao forced the emperor to go to Yongning Buddhist Temple, killed the prince, and also killed Duke of the State of the Grandee and Prince of Huaiyang Yu and left vice director and Prince of Fanyang Hui.
idiomatic: Zhao forced the emperor to Yongning Buddhist Temple, killed the prince, and also killed Yu, state grandee and prince of Huaiyang, and Hui, left vice director and prince of Fanyang.

literal: On wushen day Yuan Ye proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On wushen Yuan Ye proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

literal: Erzhu Dulü himself garrisoned the capital.
idiomatic: Erzhu Dulü took personal command of the capital garrison.

literal: On jiayin day Erzhu Zhao moved the emperor to Jinyang;
idiomatic: On jiayin Erzhu Zhao moved the emperor to Jinyang;

literal: on jiazi day he died in the Three-Tier Buddhist Temple within the city, aged twenty-four.
idiomatic: on jiazi he died in the Three-Tier Buddhist Temple within the city. He was twenty-four.

literal: Prince of Chenliu Kuan was also killed.
idiomatic: Prince of Chenliu Kuan was killed as well.

literal: That month Hedouling Bufan of Hexi and Poluo Hanchang greatly defeated Erzhu Zhao at Xiurong.
idiomatic: That month Hedouling Bufan of Hexi and Poluo Hanchang routed Erzhu Zhao at Xiurong.

literal: The townsman Zhao Luozhou of Qi Province held the west city in rebellion in response to Erzhu Zhao; Inspector and Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan abandoned the city and fled.
idiomatic: Zhao Luozhou of Qi province seized the west city in rebellion in support of Erzhu Zhao; Xiao Zan, inspector and prince of Danyang, abandoned the city and fled.

literal: Administrator of Nanyang Zhao Xiuyan seized Inspector of Jing Province Li Yanzhi and acted as provincial governor himself.
idiomatic: Zhao Xiuyan, administrator of Nanyang, seized Li Yanzhi, inspector of Jing province, and acted as provincial governor himself.

literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he was given the posthumous title Emperor Wu Huai; in the first year of Taichang he was again given the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhuang, temple name Jingzong.
idiomatic: In Zhongxing year 2 he received the posthumous title Emperor Wu Huai; in Taichang year 1 he was again given Emperor Xiaozhuang, with temple name Jingzong.

literal: In the eleventh month he was buried at Jing Mausoleum.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was interred at Jing Mausoleum.

literal: The historian says: From the end of the Xiaochang era in Wei, the realm was in turmoil; foreign insult and internal disorder alike showed that the sacred vessel would soon lack a lord.
idiomatic: The historian writes: From the close of the Xiaochang era the Wei realm was in turmoil; foreign raids and civil war alike showed that the throne would soon stand empty.

literal: Emperor Zhuang secretly planned change, recruited men to restore the throne, and though the times were desperately hard, in the end he held the four seas.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang secretly planned reform, rallied loyal armies, and though the times were desperate, in the end he held the realm.

literal: When the treacherous rebels had been cut down, the powerful usurped command—this should have been the season for Zhao to plot and exercise wisdom, for labor and modest vigilance evening and morning.
idiomatic: When the traitors were cut down, the mighty seized command—this should have been the hour for careful counsel and modest vigilance day and night.

literal: No long-rein policy was heard of; suddenly deep fear of being stabbed in the back arose; counsel was rare and art lacking, appointments went to the wrong men, suspicion led to executions, and calamity followed without pause.
idiomatic: He heard no counsel for holding the reins long; suspicion and executions followed one another, appointments went awry, and disaster came without respite.

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!

literal: That the Hu barbarians should become a scourge—was it only in the decline of Zhou and the end of Jin!
idiomatic: That the Hu should become a scourge—was it only in Zhou's decline and Jin's end!

literal: As for Gaozu going un-sacrificed and Wuxuan enjoying the temple, the three empresses descending to witness—all showed that fortune and blessing would not long endure.
idiomatic: When Gaozu went unsacrificed and Wuxuan received the temple, and the three empresses bore witness from on high, fortune could not long endure.

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Collation notes

literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Yu: in all editions "Yu" is written "Min."
idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Yu: every edition writes "Yu" as "Min."

literal: Comment: the Biography of Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan in juan 21, part 1, states: "His son Yu, styled Zichun, at the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign met disaster at Heyin."
idiomatic: The Biography of Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan in juan 21, part 1, reads: "His son Yu, styled Zichun, at the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign met disaster at Heyin."

literal: Han-Wei-Northern Dynasties tomb epitaphs collected and explained
idiomatic: Han-Wei-Northern Dynasties Tomb Epitaphs: Collected and Explained

literal: (hereafter abbreviated Tomb Epitaphs Collected)
idiomatic: (abbreviated Tomb Epitaphs Collected)

literal: contains the epitaph of Yuan Yu
idiomatic: contains the epitaph of Yuan Yu

literal: (plate 173, no. 2)
idiomatic: (plate 173, no. 2)

literal: —this is the man.
idiomatic: —this is the man in question.

literal: "Yu" and "Chun" in the name correspond; "Min" is a graphic corruption from similarity of form—now emended.
idiomatic: "Yu" pairs with "Chun" in the name; "Min" is a graphic corruption from similar forms—emended here.

literal: succeeded to the rank of Baron of Tailin with an open state: in the Baina, Southern, Northern, and Bureau editions "Tai" is all written "Qin"; the Jibu edition further corrupts it to "Zou"; the Palace edition according to juan 101 Biography of Gaochang
idiomatic: Succeeded as baron of Tailin with an open state: in the Baina, Southern, Northern, and Bureau editions "Tai" is written "Qin" throughout; the Jibu edition corrupts it further to "Zou"; the Palace edition follows juan 101, Biography of Gaochang,

literal: (supplement)
idiomatic: (supplement)

literal: to emend "Tai."
idiomatic: to emend "Tai."

literal: Comment: Beishi juan 5 Yuan version
idiomatic: Beishi juan 5, Yuan version,

literal: (the base text of the Baina edition)
idiomatic: (base text of the Baina edition)

literal: and the Southern and Northern Directorate editions also read "Qin"; the Baina edition according to the Palace edition emended "Tai."
idiomatic: and the Southern and Northern Directorate editions also read "Qin"; the Baina edition follows the Palace edition in reading "Tai."

literal: Comment: this biography reads "Tai," and the entry for the tenth month of the second year of Yongxi in juan 11 Annals of the Deposed Emperor also reads "Tai"—now follow the Palace edition.
idiomatic: This biography reads "Tai," and the Yongxi year 2, tenth-month entry in juan 11, Annals of the Deposed Emperor, also reads "Tai"—the Palace reading is followed here.

literal: military grade from third rank and above, and those on campaign from fourth rank, receive one major grade of preferment: Cefu juan 62
idiomatic: Military grade from third rank and above and those on campaign from fourth rank receive one major grade of preferment: Cefu juan 62

literal: under "on campaign" there are no characters "fourth rank."
idiomatic: under "on campaign" the words "fourth rank" do not appear.

literal: Comment: with the characters "fourth rank" present the sense is obscure—suspected interpolation, or there is lacuna under "on campaign."
idiomatic: With "fourth rank" present the sense is obscure—likely an interpolation, or text is missing after "on campaign."

literal: that month: Comment: "that month" already appears above and should not recur—suspected interpolation.
idiomatic: "That month": "that month" already appears above and should not recur—likely an interpolation.

literal: Administrator of Mount Tai Yang Kan held the commandery and led Liang general Wang Bian to attack Yan Province: in all editions "Wang Bian" is written "Wang Sengbian."
idiomatic: Yang Kan, administrator of Mount Tai, held the commandery and led Liang general Wang Bian against Yan province: all editions write "Wang Bian" as "Wang Sengbian."

literal: Comment: the Biography of Yang Yu in juan 58 narrates this affair as "Wang Bian"; the Biography of Yang Kan in Liang shu juan 33 states that after Kan surrendered to Liang, "he sent Yang Yaren and Wang Ban to lead troops to meet him."
idiomatic: The Biography of Yang Yu in juan 58 gives "Wang Bian"; Liang shu juan 33, Biography of Yang Kan, says that after Kan surrendered to Liang he "sent Yang Yaren and Wang Ban to lead troops to meet him."

literal: Clearly "Wang Bian" or "Wang Ban" is this annal's "Wang Sengbian."
idiomatic: Clearly "Wang Bian" or "Wang Ban" in those texts is this annal's "Wang Sengbian."

literal: "Wang Bian" also appears repeatedly in juan 21, part 2, Biography of Prince of Pengcheng Xie with appended Biography of Yuan Shao, juan 79 Biography of Lu Yue, and elsewhere.
idiomatic: "Wang Bian" also appears repeatedly in juan 21, part 2 (Biography of Prince of Pengcheng Xie, appended Biography of Yuan Shao), juan 79 (Biography of Lu Yue), and elsewhere.

literal: Examination shows that the Biography of Wang Sengbian in Liang shu juan 45 does not record this affair.
idiomatic: The Biography of Wang Sengbian in Liang shu juan 45 does not record this affair.

literal: That biography states that when Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong, was inspector of Jing Province, Sengbian served under Xiao Yi.
idiomatic: That biography says that when Xiao Yi, prince of Xiangdong, was inspector of Jing province, Sengbian served under him.

literal: According to the Annals of Emperor Yuan in Liang shu juan 5, Xiao Yi's first appointment as inspector of Jing Province was from the seventh year of Putong
idiomatic: Liang shu juan 5, Annals of Emperor Yuan, records Xiao Yi's first appointment as inspector of Jing province from Putong year 7

literal: to the fifth year of Datong
idiomatic: through Datong year 5
